chunks: Muhammad ibn Ya'qub from Abu Ali al-Ash'ari from Muhammad ibn al-Jabbar from some of his companions from Khalaf ibn Hammad from Isma'il ibn Abi Farwa from Abu Basir said:
Abu Abdillah (peace be upon him) said: "When a man dies, his wealth becomes free (of the restriction of the deceased's debt) and whatever debt is upon him."

key_terms.أَبُو عَبْدِ اللَّهِ: Abu Abdillah (Imam al-Sadiq, peace be upon him)
key_terms.حَلَّ: became free/permissible (referring to the estate becoming available for distribution after debt settlement)

ai.seo_question: What happens to a deceased person's wealth and debts according to Shia jurisprudence?
ai.summary: In the context of *Tahdhib al-Ahkam*, this hadith clarifies the immediate legal status of the deceased's estate, emphasizing that debts are a prior claim on the assets before distribution to heirs. This ruling underscores the Shia jurisprudential principle that the settlement of liabilities (*al-dayn*) takes precedence over inheritance shares, ensuring creditors' rights are protected. It reflects the practical application of estate liquidation where the 'hal' (available) wealth is directly applied to clear obligations.
